items.claim: FY25 revenue growth guided at roughly 13% at the midpoint, though the recovery has been uneven quarter to quarter (strong in Q1/Q2, stepped down in Q3).
items.quote: the midpoint for '25 is somewhere around 13% growth
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Industrial and automotive together make up about 70% of TI's business and both are recovering, with industrial's recovery more significant in percentage terms but still below its 2022 revenue peak.
items.quote: about 70% of our business are industrial and automotive
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Starting with the January fiscal '26 earnings call, TI will report data center as a standalone fifth end market alongside industrial, automotive, personal electronics, and comms.
items.quote: we'll provide data center as a stand-alone market
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Data center revenue is currently around $1.2 billion for analog and embedded combined, growing well above 50%, with management suggesting it could become a double-digit or even ~20% share of TAM long term.
items.quote: Most exciting is the growth rate is well above 50%.
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Management explained the guided gross margin step-down is tied to reduced factory loadings, because TI has stopped building inventory at the prior pace after reaching its target inventory level.
items.quote: we are stopping building inventory at the same rate
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: FY26 CapEx is expected in the $2 billion-$3 billion range, down from $5 billion in FY25, as TI nears the end of its 2021-2026 six-year investment cycle.
items.quote: a $2.5 billion to $3 billion of CapEx opportunity
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: For FY27, if demand doesn't require further capacity, CapEx could fall to a 'maintenance mode' level, cited as roughly 4% of revenue based on TI's prior ramp experience.
items.quote: maybe 4% of revenue or something like that
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: TI is internalizing back-end assembly/test capacity: front-end (fab) internalization is already about 90% heading to 95% by decade end, while OSAT internalization rose from below 60% to near 80% this year, aspiring above 90% by decade end.
items.quote: By the end of the decade, we'll be at 95%.
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Management reiterated its free cash flow target range of $8 billion to $12 billion, framing $12 billion as low probability (would require $26 billion revenue) but $8 billion as plausible.
items.quote: we put a target there of $8 billion to $12 billion
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Management reaffirmed the long-term commitment to return the vast majority of free cash flow to shareholders, noting TI has been willing to return above 100% of free cash flow opportunistically, including in 2025.
items.quote: returning at above 100% where we saw an opportunity
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Management traced historical analog market share loss (peak-to-trough about 400bps, of which ~150bps has been regained) to being capacity-constrained during the prior upcycle, when new fab capacity took about 3 years to build.
items.quote: the lead time to build new capacity was like 3 years
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Embedded segment share loss (roughly half lost since 2017) is attributed to prior portfolio strategy weakness rather than supply constraints, and management says early signs of stabilization are appearing as the newer embedded portfolio gets designed in.
items.quote: we saw a gradual share loss since 2017
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: China represents about 20% of both the addressable market and TI's business; management addressed the risk that heavy U.S. manufacturing investment could disadvantage TI in China, citing existing non-U.S. manufacturing footprint (China, Europe, Japan) as a mitigant.
items.quote: China is about 20% of our -- of the market
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Management acknowledged that further U.S.-China decoupling over the next 5-10 years is a reasonable base case, while maintaining a belief that TI can continue shipping analog and embedded parts into China.
items.quote: some more decoupling between the U.S. and China
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: TI's China business is growing nicely this year, described as 'low 30%' year-to-date, with continued design-in momentum attributed to dependable local capacity and service level.
items.quote: Our business in China is growing nicely this year.
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: Management noted TI has competed directly with local Chinese competitors since 2018, and that adapting the company's culture around speed, cost discipline, and urgency to compete there has also benefited TI's competitiveness in other geographies.
items.quote: competing with the local competition since 2018
items.speaker: CEO

items.claim: On M&A criteria, management said any deal must have strong strategic fit: buildable/synergistic in-house, broad portfolio and customer base, weighted toward industrial/automotive over personal electronics, and skewed toward analog mixed-signal rather than large MCUs or high-concentration processors.
items.quote: does it have a good strategic fit for the company
items.speaker: CEO

qa_flags.question: Analyst pressed on whether CapEx could be taken down further into FY27 given the inventory and capacity build-out already achieved.
qa_flags.response_pattern: CEO declined to give a precise FY27 number ('I can't be talking about precision'), deferred specifics to the February capital management call, and tied the outcome to unspecified future revenue.

qa_flags.question: Analyst asked directly whether next year (FY26) could be a record free cash flow year.
qa_flags.response_pattern: CEO repeated the existing $8B-$12B target range but explicitly said 'we are not going to force it' to hit $8B, adding the outlook 'can change every quarter' rather than committing to a number.

qa_flags.question: Analyst repeatedly asked about the shape/trajectory of the demand recovery and relative end-market strength heading into December.
qa_flags.response_pattern: CEO twice declined to characterize the shape of the recovery, stating TI has 'given up on trying to call the shape of the recovery' and will only report results after each quarter closes.
